page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c7t.large is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance running on the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel Xeon 8369B processor operating at 2.7 GHz. The instance is configured with 2 dedicated vCPUs derived from 1 physical core with hyper-threading enabled. It includes 4.0 GB of system memory, providing a 2.0 GB per core ratio. There is no local storage or GPU hardware bundled with this instance, and network connectivity is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark results indicate moderate single-core performance but limited multi-core scaling. The stress-ng single-core CPU performance is rated as average at 1890.38, while the multi-core performance drops to a poor rating of 1934.88. Memory bandwidth is relatively constrained, with read-only large block speeds at 10.57 GB/sec and write large block speeds at 12.34 GB/sec. Single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression perform at average levels, reaching 28.01 GB/sec and 10.87 GB/sec respectively. However, database and transactional workloads show weaker performance, with Redis SET operations achieving 1.98 million operations per second and Passmark database operations scoring 1017.6.

Given its dedicated CPU allocation and 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, this instance is designed for entry-level compute-intensive tasks rather than memory-heavy or storage-bound applications. The lack of local storage means all storage must be network-attached, which, combined with the 2 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, may limit high-throughput data operations. It is best suited for lightweight web serving, single-threaded batch processing, and basic utility workloads that benefit from dedicated Intel Xeon CPU execution but do not require large memory footprints or high multi-threaded performance.
